extracted.intended_audience: Video journalists, solo video journalists, video editors, reporters/field producers, and broadcast stations submitting to the NPPA Best of Photojournalism 2026 Video Photojournalism and Editing Division
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluation criteria for submitting and judging video photojournalism and editing work to the NPPA Best of Photojournalism 2026 competition, including individual story categories, entrant eligibility, technical specs, and compilation ('- of the Year' / Station) requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary judging criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges will evaluate entries based on technical excellence, storytelling, and demonstrated journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The critical factor will be the quality of the journalism and the audience’s ability to understand the story. The contest acknowledges both reporting and editing roles in shaping narrative and final story impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: journalistic distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: All entries must have been created for journalistic distribution through broadcast or online channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsored content or work created for non-journalistic entities is not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft contest / single-person recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a craft contest. All entrants are one person being recognized, except for the Station Of The Year categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should reflect the individual entrant's craft unless entering Station Of The Year, which recognizes a staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entrant category — Video Journalist (VJ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists working as members of a newsroom staff or as independent photographers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For categories where filming is judged, at least 90% of the video must be filmed by the entrant (unless otherwise specified).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entrant category — Solo Video Journalist (SVJ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists responsible for filming, reporting, writing, tracking, and editing their stories daily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must have filmed at least 90% of the video and be the sole editor (unless otherwise specified). “Nat Sound” packages (stories without a reporter track) are not allowed for SVJs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entrant category — Editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists who craft the story in the edit and are solely responsible for every action in the editing process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For editing-focused categories, it does not matter who filmed the video.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entrant category — Reporter / Field Producer
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters and field producers who, in collaboration with a visual journalist, produce outstanding visual stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Solo Video Journalist can be considered a Reporter / Field Producer in this contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filming ownership threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: For categories where filming is judged, at least 90% of the content must be recorded by the entrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions apply only where otherwise specified in a category. Some specialty categories require write-ups documenting elements not personally created or captured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry limits per individual
rubrics_metrics.description: A maximum of 4 entries per individual is allowed in each story category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals may submit an entry to each “- of the Year” award for which they are eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Station of the Year submission limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Each station may submit only one Station of the Year entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No other compilation entries are allowed from the station.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-air identification policy
rubrics_metrics.description: On-air identification (for example, “With photographer John Doe…”) does not need to be edited out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants may leave normal on-air credits intact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical file requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All entries should be compressed for smooth playback online. Videos must be mp4 format at 1080p resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Entry Rules and Guidelines for full technical submission instructions and contact competition staff with questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline News (Breaking & Deadline category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Breaking News or General News stories recorded, edited, and broadcast within four consecutive hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The entry may be a package or include a live shot. If a live shot is included, the unedited air check must be submitted. Filming: 90% of the content must be recorded by the entrant. Max runtime: 5 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live (Breaking & Deadline category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any live broadcast recorded by an individual photojournalist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries are judged solely on the live section and the ability to convey the scene visually. The entrant must have controlled all live video. Filming: 90% recorded by entrant. Max runtime: 5 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaking News (unscheduled)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unscheduled and unfolding news events recorded, edited, and broadcast within 12 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This category recognizes the ability to perform effectively under high pressure. Filming: 90% recorded by entrant. Max runtime: 5 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily News — Hard
rubrics_metrics.description: A time-sensitive, significant news story covering a planned or unplanned event with a serious, factual tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries must be recorded, edited, and broadcast within 24 hours. Filming: 90% recorded by entrant. Max runtime: 5 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily News — Light
rubrics_metrics.description: A news story with a lighter tone, often highlighting unique, community-focused topics, typically produced with little pre-planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries must be recorded, edited, and broadcast within 24 hours. Filming: 90% recorded by entrant. Max runtime: 5 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 60-Minute Edit (timed editing challenge)
rubrics_metrics.description: A timed challenge to edit a complete news story in 60 minutes or less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The clock begins when the first element is placed on the timeline. Entries are judged on storytelling, creativity, and technical skill achieved under the deadline. This category prioritizes editing of the story and it does not matter where the content originates. Max runtime: 5 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Feature — Hard
rubrics_metrics.description: A planned, thoughtful, and impactful news feature with a serious tone that appeals to the viewer’s emotional side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics may include societal issues or human struggles. Filming: 90% recorded by entrant. Max runtime: 10 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Feature — Light
rubrics_metrics.description: A planned news feature with a lighter, uplifting, or humorous tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This category is for engaging, heartwarming, or entertaining stories. Filming: 90% recorded by entrant. Max runtime: 10 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sports Feature
rubrics_metrics.description: A feature story about the emotional, human side of sports, as opposed to direct coverage of a competition or highlights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filming: 90% recorded by entrant. Max runtime: 10 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative (Specialty)
rubrics_metrics.description: A well-researched, enterprising investigative report where the visual storytelling elevates a story that uncovers important issues or holds the powerful accountable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must include a write-up detailing any elements they did not personally create or capture. Max runtime: 15 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects Edit (Specialty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must demonstrate the effective use of visual effects to enhance storytelling in a meaningful way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must include a write-up detailing any elements they did not personally create or capture. Max runtime: 15 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-Form (Specialty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compelling narratives that demonstrate a substantial commitment of time and effort, including in-depth features and investigative reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must include a write-up detailing any elements they did not personally create or capture. Max runtime: 15 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural Sound-Driven (Specialty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that rely solely on natural sound, sound bites, and/or music to engage viewers; narration is not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must include a write-up detailing any elements they did not personally create or capture. Max runtime: 15 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: ‘- of the Year’ reel format and content limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries for all “- of the Year” awards are compiled into a single compilation reel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reel format: single compilation reel with a maximum runtime of 25 minutes. Reel content: minimum of 6 and maximum of 8 stories. A maximum of two stories from any single category may be used. Entries must be submitted in the same order as the required competition categories listed above.

rubrics_metrics.name: ‘- of the Year’ eligibility and finalist qualification (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility typically requires entering at least six stories across the individual categories. To be considered a finalist, the entrant must place in at least two individual categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The stories that must be included on the compilation reel are those that place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photojournalist of the Year mandatory content & documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reel must demonstrate a range of skills and meet submission/documentation rules for Photojournalist of the Year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility: open to entrants competing as video journalists who enter at least six stories. Reel format: single compilation reel max 25 minutes. Reel content: 6–8 stories, max two per category. Mandatory: include at least one story from Breaking & Deadline, one from Daily News, and one from Features or Specialty. Required documentation: a text document listing each story’s title, original contest category, and total run time in order. Craft write-up: brief write-up explaining how the stories showcase the entrant's craft and approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor of the Year mandatory content & documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reel and documentation requirements for Editor of the Year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility: open to all entrants entering at least six stories. Reel must include a 60-minute Edit, one story from Daily News, one from Features, and one from Specialty categories. Reel format and documentation same as other ‘- of the Year’ awards. Craft write-up explaining how the stories showcase the entrant's craft as a Video Editor is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solo Video Journalist of the Year mandatory content & documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reel and documentation requirements for Solo Video Journalist of the Year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility: open to entrants competing as Solo Video Journalists who enter at least six stories. Reel must demonstrate range, include at least one story from Breaking & Deadline, one from Daily News, and one from Features or Specialty. Documentation and craft write-up required, as with other ‘- of the Year’ awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporter of the Year scope & requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Honors a Reporter or Field Producer who excels in writing, interviewing, and collaborating with visual journalists to produce outstanding visual stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility: open to reporters, field producers, or Solo Journalists with at least six stories across individual categories. Finalist qualification: entrant must be the credited reporter on at least one story that places; that story must be included on the compilation reel. Reel format, content limits (6–8 stories, max two per category), documentation, and craft write-up requirements apply. Judging focuses on integration of reporting and writing with visual storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Station of the Year content & format
rubrics_metrics.description: Station-level award recognizing a local broadcast station’s photography staff; submission is a single compilation entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format: single compilation entry max runtime 40 minutes. Content: stations must submit at least two stories in each meta-category (Breaking & Deadline; Daily News; Features or Specialty Coverage). Required documentation: a document listing all stories in order, including names of the photojournalists, categories, run times, and the total number of eligible photojournalists on staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Station of the Year staff representation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules determining what portion of a station’s photography staff must be represented on the Station of the Year entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For stations with a photography staff of 14 or fewer, at least one-half of the staff must be represented. For stations with a photography staff of 15 or more, at least one-third of the staff must be represented. A single Video Journalist, Solo Video Journalist, Editor, or Reporter may not contribute more than three stories to a Station of the Year entry. For staff counts, include anyone who regularly shoots video (including SVJs); do not include producers or editors who only shoot occasionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy Statement requirement (Station of the Year)
rubrics_metrics.description: Station entries must be accompanied by a short (one-page maximum) statement addressing the station's philosophy and contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement should cover: your staff’s philosophy on video photojournalism; how your staff tries to elevate the industry and think outside the box; how the staff contributes daily and how they contributed to the reel; the philosophy of this specific SOY entry (e.g., how you pushed your comfort zones); why you feel your staff should win; and anything else you want the judges to know.
